question: Should OpenClaw accept `currentTokenCount` plus the new token-budget helper exports as the stable public ContextEngine/plugin SDK contract now, or fold this token-budget signal into the broader assemble metadata RFC at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/82137?
rationale: The diff is mostly coherent, but it promotes new public plugin API surface and SDK exports that can constrain third-party context-engine implementations while adjacent assemble metadata work remains open.

options.title: Accept Narrow Contract After Proof
options.body: Approve the `currentTokenCount` contract now, then require SDK baseline regeneration and redacted real-behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Fold Into RFC
options.body: Pause this branch and handle token counts together with the broader provenance/internal-event assemble metadata design.

options.title: Keep Helpers Private For Now
options.body: Avoid new SDK runtime exports until the permanent plugin-facing token-budget helper contract is settled.

recommendation.title: Accept Narrow Contract After Proof
recommendation.body: Approve the `currentTokenCount` contract now, then require SDK baseline regeneration and redacted real-behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned to the PR and have the strongest recent current-main history on the context-engine contract and token-budget paths.
